title: Other places heard: Preservation, Harmony and parades
summary: He has been at Preservation almost nightly, played parades and sat in with Kid Sheik; the Harmony Hall was only dance music apart from one pianist.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Did you hear any other bands since you've been here?

Oh yeah, I've been, I would say I've been at preservation almost every night. I've also been to Dixler and all, I've been to Harmony and I've been with the Sheik at a few jobs. And at the parties and I played some parades. So I had a session too with this Japanese fellow, a recording session.
What about the Harmony and what was that like?
Oh it was just dance music. It wasn't really jazz. The only thing that sounded any good was Sing, the piano player. Sing Melo? Yeah, he sounded pretty good.
Yeah, I like his playing too.

Actually he sounded similar to Alton Pennell in some ways. Except that's when he was playing with the melody with a few things between. But when he tried to play a real solo, it kind of broke close too much. When he did what? When he tried to play an improviser all through a solo. He just couldn't keep it together. It didn't sound very well. I see.
